title: nf-core/spatiallattice pipeline parameters
description: pipeline for processing and integration of MACSima multiplexed imaging with H&E stained tissue slides

input_output_options.title: Input/output options
input_output_options.description: Define where the pipeline should find input data and save output data.

input.description: Path to comma-separated file containing information about the samples in the experiment.
input.help_text: You will need to create a design file with information about the samples in your experiment before running the pipeline. Use this parameter to specify its location. It has to be a comma-separated file with 2 columns, and a header row. See [usage docs](https://nf-co.re/spatiallattice/usage#samplesheet-input).

project.description: Set to true to run processing steps on a full project or study with multiple experiments and ROIs. Use when providing the samplesheet for a ful project or study.
project.help_text: Enable this option if you are providing a samplesheet for a full project or study with multiple experiments and ROIs. See the example samplesheet_project.

illumination_correction.description: Give this flag to apply illumination correction to all tiles, the illumination profiles are calculated with basicpy.
illumination_correction.help_text: Enable this option to run the optional illumination correction step on the input images with basicpy.

hi_exposure_only.description: Give this flag to extract only the set of images with the highest exposure time.
hi_exposure_only.help_text: Enable this option to extract only the set of images with the highest exposure time. All downstream processing steps will use only the high exposure images.

remove_reference_marker.description: mark the removal of the reference marker ,e.g. DAPI, for all cycles except the first one.
remove_reference_marker.help_text: mark the removal of the reference marker ,e.g. DAPI, for all cycles except the first one.

qc_metrics.description: measure features of contrast, intensity and sharpness of each tile in the cycle and appends them to a table.
qc_metrics.help_text: measure features of contrast, intensity and sharpness of each tile in the cycle and appends them to a table.

write_table.description: Writes a table with the acquisition parameters, metadata and,if enabled, qc metrics of each tile.
write_table.help_text: Writes a table with the acquisition parameters, metadata and,if enabled, qc metrics of each tile.

background_subtraction.description: Performs pixel-by-pixel background subtraction between marker and background channels scaled by their respective exposure times.
background_subtraction.help_text: Performs pixel-by-pixel background subtraction between marker and background channels scaled by their respective exposure times.

stainsegmy.description: Run nuclei segmentation on provided H&E images.
stainsegmy.help_text: Run nuclei segmentation on provided H&E images.

segmentation.description: Comma-separated list of segmentation tools to run on the MACSima image (cellpose3, cellpose4, mesmer).
segmentation.help_text: Select one or more segmentation tools, separated by commas, e.g. `--segmentation cellpose4,mesmer`. Available tools: `cellpose3` (Cellpose 3), `cellpose4` (Cellpose 4 / Cellpose-SAM) and `mesmer` (DeepCell Mesmer). Segmentation runs on the ASHLAR output, or on the background-subtracted image if `--background_subtraction` is enabled. In that case, channel indices refer to the background-subtracted image, where background channels have been removed. Set to an empty string to skip segmentation.

cellpose3_pretrained_model.description: Cellpose model to use for cell segmentation.
cellpose3_pretrained_model.help_text: Pretrained Cellpose 3 model (e.g. `nuclei`, `cyto3`). Used when no custom model is given. Set to `none` to use the built-in default model of the Cellpose version.

cellpose3_custom_model.description: Path to custom Cellpose model to use for cell segmentation.
cellpose3_custom_model.help_text: Specify the path to a custom Cellpose model to use for cell segmentation. If this is set, the pretrained model will be ignored.

cellpose3_save_flows.description: whether or not to save RGB images of flows when masks are saved.
cellpose3_save_flows.help_text: whether or not to save RGB images of flows when masks are saved.

cellpose3_diameter.description: Expected object diameter in pixels used to rescale the image to the model's training diameter (17 px for the nuclei model, 30 px for cyto models)
cellpose3_diameter.help_text: Expected object diameter in pixels. Cellpose rescales the image so objects match the training diameter of the model (about 17 px for `nuclei`, 30 px for `cyto*` models).

cellpose3_chan.description: Cellpose channel to use for cell segmentation.
cellpose3_chan.help_text: Specify the Cellpose channel to use for cell segmentation. This is the channel index of the image to use for segmentation. The default is 0, which is the first channel.

cellpose3_chan2.description: Cellpose second channel to use for cell segmentation.
cellpose3_chan2.help_text: Specify the Cellpose second channel to use for cell segmentation. This is the channel index of the second image to use for segmentation. The default is null, which means that no second channel will be used.

cellpose3_flow_threshold.description: Name of the flow error threshold to use for cell segmentation.
cellpose3_flow_threshold.help_text: Flow error threshold. 0 turns off this optional QC step. Default: 0.4

cellpose4_pretrained_model.description: Cellpose 4 (Cellpose-SAM) pretrained model to use for cell segmentation.
cellpose4_pretrained_model.help_text: Pretrained Cellpose 4 (Cellpose-SAM) model (e.g. `cpsam`). Used when no custom model is given. Set to `none` to use the built-in default model of the Cellpose version.

cellpose4_custom_model.description: Path to custom Cellpose 4 (Cellpose-SAM) model to use for cell segmentation.
cellpose4_custom_model.help_text: Specify the path to a custom Cellpose 4 (Cellpose-SAM) model to use for cell segmentation. If this is set, the pretrained model will be ignored.

cellpose4_save_flows.help_text: Whether to save the flows of Cellpose 4 as tif in addition to the masks.

cellpose4_diameter.description: Expected object diameter in pixels for Cellpose 4.
cellpose4_diameter.help_text: Expected object diameter in pixels. If not set, Cellpose 4 uses its default. Set to 0 to estimate the diameter automatically.

cellpose4_flow_threshold.help_text: Flow error threshold (Cellpose default: 0.4). 0 turns off this optional QC step.

mesmer_image_mpp.description: Resolution of the image in microns per pixel used by Mesmer.
mesmer_image_mpp.help_text: Microns per pixel of the input image. Mesmer rescales the image to the resolution of its training data (0.5 mpp).

mesmer_compartment.help_text: Segment nuclei (`nuclear`), whole cells (`whole-cell`, requires `--mesmer_membrane_channel`) or both.

mesmer_nuclear_channel.description: 0-based channel index of the nuclear marker used by Mesmer.
mesmer_nuclear_channel.help_text: 0-based channel index of the nuclear marker (e.g. DAPI) in the multichannel image.

mesmer_membrane_channel.description: 0-based channel index of the membrane marker used by Mesmer.
mesmer_membrane_channel.help_text: 0-based channel index of the membrane marker in the multichannel image. Required for `whole-cell` or `both` compartments.

stainwarpy.description: Run the StainWarPy registration step to register the H&E image (moving) to the immunofluorescence image (fixed).
stainwarpy.help_text: Enable this option to run the optional StainWarPy registration step. This registers the H&E image to the immunofluorescence image using stainwarpy.

fixed_img.description: Channel of the fixed image to be used for registration. 0-based index or string h, e or d to convert H&E into Hematoxylin, Eosin or DAB.
fixed_img.help_text: 0-based index of the channel of the fixed image to be used for registration. If a string is given (h, e or d) it converts the H&E image into Hematoxylin, Eosin or DAB.

final_sz.description: Image resolution in micrometers to be used for applying the registration scheme.
final_sz.help_text: Image resolution in micrometers (microns per pixel) to be used for applying the registration scheme. Should be at least 2-3 times smaller than the registration feature size.

rami2d.description: Run the RAMI2D registration step to register the H&E image (moving) to the immunofluorescence image (fixed).
rami2d.help_text: Enable this option to run the optional RAMI2D registration step. This registers the H&E image to the immunofluorescence image using rami2d-register.

rami2d_mpp_fix.description: Pixel size in micrometers of the fixed image.
rami2d_mpp_fix.help_text: Pixel size in micrometers (microns per pixel) of the fixed image used for registration.

rami2d_ifix.description: Channel of the fixed image to be used for registration. 0-based index or string h, e or d to convert H&E into Hematoxylin, Eosin or DAB.
rami2d_ifix.help_text: 0-based index of the channel of the fixed image to be used for registration. If a string is given (h, e or d) it converts the H&E image into Hematoxylin, Eosin or DAB.

rami2d_mpp_mov.description: Pixel size in micrometers of the moving image.
rami2d_mpp_mov.help_text: Pixel size in micrometers (microns per pixel) of the moving image used for registration.

rami2d_imov.description: Channel of the moving image to be used for registration. 0-based index or string h, e or d to convert H&E into Hematoxylin, Eosin or DAB.
rami2d_imov.help_text: 0-based index of the channel of the moving image to be used for registration. If a string is given (h, e or d) it converts the H&E image into Hematoxylin, Eosin or DAB.

rami2d_mpp_reg.description: Image resolution in micrometers to be used for applying the registration scheme.
rami2d_mpp_reg.help_text: Image resolution in micrometers (microns per pixel) to be used for applying the registration scheme. Should be at least 2-3 times smaller than the registration feature size.

rami2d_transform.description: Run the RAMI2D transform step to apply the transformation maps to images associated with the moving image.
rami2d_transform.help_text: Enable this option to run the optional RAMI2D transform step. This applies the transformation maps produced by rami2d-register to images associated with the moving image using rami2d-transform.

rami2d_transform_input.description: Path to the image to be transformed.
rami2d_transform_input.help_text: Path to the image to be transformed by rami2d-transform.

rami2d_transform_mpp.description: Pixel size in micrometers of the image to be transformed.
rami2d_transform_mpp.help_text: Pixel size in micrometers (microns per pixel) of the image to be transformed.

rami2d_transform_tdir.description: Path to the folder with the transformation map files (.txt).
rami2d_transform_tdir.help_text: Path to the folder containing the transformation map files (.txt) produced by rami2d-register.

outdir.description: The output directory where the results will be saved. You have to use absolute paths to storage on Cloud infrastructure.

email.help_text: Set this parameter to your e-mail address to get a summary e-mail with details of the run sent to you when the workflow exits. If set in your user config file (`~/.nextflow/config`) then you don't need to specify this on the command line for every run.

multiqc_title.description: MultiQC report title. Printed as page header, used for filename if not otherwise specified.

institutional_config_options.title: Institutional config options
institutional_config_options.description: Parameters used to describe centralised config profiles. These should not be edited.
institutional_config_options.help_text: The centralised nf-core configuration profiles use a handful of pipeline parameters to describe themselves. This information is then printed to the Nextflow log when you run a pipeline. You should not need to change these values when you run a pipeline.

custom_config_version.description: Git commit id for Institutional configs.

custom_config_base.help_text: If you're running offline, Nextflow will not be able to fetch the institutional config files from the internet. If you don't need them, then this is not a problem. If you do need them, you should download the files from the repo and tell Nextflow where to find them with this parameter.

generic_options.title: Generic options
generic_options.description: Less common options for the pipeline, typically set in a config file.
generic_options.help_text:
These options are common to all nf-core pipelines and allow you to customise some of the core preferences for how the pipeline runs.

Typically these options would be set in a Nextflow config file loaded for all pipeline runs, such as `~/.nextflow/config`.

publish_dir_mode.description: Method used to save pipeline results to output directory.
publish_dir_mode.help_text: The Nextflow `publishDir` option specifies which intermediate files should be saved to the output directory. This option tells the pipeline what method should be used to move these files. See [Nextflow docs](https://www.nextflow.io/docs/latest/process.html#publishdir) for details.

email_on_fail.description: Email address for completion summary, only when pipeline fails.
email_on_fail.help_text: An email address to send a summary email to when the pipeline is completed - ONLY sent if the pipeline does not exit successfully.

plaintext_email.description: Send plain-text email instead of HTML.

max_multiqc_email_size.description: File size limit when attaching MultiQC reports to summary emails.

monochrome_logs.description: Do not use coloured log outputs.

multiqc_config.description: Custom config file to supply to MultiQC.

multiqc_logo.description: Custom logo file to supply to MultiQC. File name must also be set in the MultiQC config file

multiqc_methods_description.description: Custom MultiQC yaml file containing HTML including a methods description.

validate_params.description: Boolean whether to validate parameters against the schema at runtime

pipelines_testdata_base_path.description: Base URL or local path to location of pipeline test dataset files

trace_report_suffix.description: Suffix to add to the trace report filename. Default is the date and time in the format yyyy-MM-dd_HH-mm-ss.

help_full.description: Display the full detailed help message.

show_hidden.description: Display hidden parameters in the help message (only works when --help or --help_full are provided).
